facts.label: Debt, liquidity and covenant evidence located
facts.text: - Debt note: the Q3 statements list Senior Credit Facility: borrowings and 6.875% senior notes due 2029 and reconcile the movement in long-term debt (pages 8 and 9). No current portion of long-term debt line appears on the balance sheet (page:1). - Liquidity table: Q3 report pages 12 and 13 give the facility, its availability and maturity. The senior credit facility matures October 31, 2028, with a footnote that US$43 million will expire on June 28, 2027. (page:13). The operating and demand letter of credit facilities are secured; the senior notes are unsecured, per the same table. - Covenants: the senior credit facility tests a leverage ratio of senior secured debt to covenant EBITDA and an interest coverage ratio, with reported values in the covenant table (Q3 report page:13 and Q3 statements page:9). The notes carry an incurrence-based interest coverage test described on page:13 of the Q3 report. Reported covenant values exist for March 31, 2026 (page:10 of the Q1 report), June 30, 2026 (page:8 of the Q2 statements) and September 30, 2026. - Fair value of the notes is disclosed in Note 11 (page:11 of the Q3 statements). - Contingency: a Canada Revenue Agency reassessment matter with a stated maximum exposure and a requirement to pay part of any assessed amount while contested is described in the Q3 report (pages 11 and 12) and in Note 12 of the Q3 statements (pages 12 and 13). It first appears as a subsequent event in the Q2 release (page:6). - Capital commitments are in Note 10 (page:11 of the Q3 statements) and the Q3 report (page:8).

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported financial base is usable for the current-period credit view at the level of consolidated quarterly statements, but it is built on unaudited interim reports and a single year-end balance sheet, so every annual figure used here is assembled from quarters rather than read from an annual statement. Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA grew in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025, while nine-month Adjusted EBITDA is lower than the prior-year nine months, because of lower upfront capital payments in Canada, higher operating costs in the United States and internationally, and higher share-based compensation (R3 page:5). Debt is a single secured revolving facility drawn in US dollars and one series of US dollar unsecured senior notes, with no current portion of long-term debt on the balance sheet. Because the debt is US dollar denominated and the statements are in Canadian dollars, reported debt moves with the exchange rate independently of repayment. Leverage computed from reported figures is steady and moderate, interest cover on a nine-month basis improved, and covenant headroom is wide. The limits are equally clear: free cash flow weakened as capital spending rose, cash is small, liquidity is revolver-dependent, a contested tax reassessment is a contingent cash call, and the annual comparators, the covenant EBITDA definition and the facility pricing are not in the pack. Every ratio below is a calculation from printed components; the issuer prints only the covenant ratios, the debt-to-capitalization ratio, working capital and the liquidity claim.

facts.label: Subsequent events and contingency story
facts.text: - In late July 2026, after the Q2 balance sheet date and before the Q2 release, the Canada Revenue Agency issued a Notice of Reassessment for the 2018 tax year denying a deduction of intercompany dividends received in a preferred share financing, with a proposal for the 2019 to 2022 tax years on the same basis (R2 page:6; S3 page:12). The issuer will object and says its filing position is appropriate. It expects reassessments for the 2019 to 2023 years over the next twenty-four months and does not expect taxes payable to be affected until the 2024 to 2027 tax years. Once reassessed it must pay half of the assessed tax and interest while the issue is resolved. Credit mechanism: a cash call that would arrive before resolution, without a recognized provision. - On October 27, 2026 the issuer raised its 2026 capital budget range and disclosed a pending customer upgrade with contracts through 2029 (R3 page:2 and page:8). Shares outstanding at that date were 12,538,736 (R3 page:14) against 12,585,648 at September 30, 2026 (S3 page:10). - With Q2 results the issuer announced a further five-year Kuwait contract for an existing rig (R2 page:2); this is a Q2 development, not an event after the Q3 balance sheet date.

facts.label: Narrative review by dimension
facts.text: - Leverage. Evidence: the leverage chart table and the debt movement reconciliation. Mechanic: debt in US dollars is revalued in Canadian dollars each period, so carrying value fell by less than the net repayment because the foreign exchange adjustment added back; EBITDA recovered in Q3 2026 while cash fell, so net leverage rose from June 30, 2026 even though debt was flat. Implication: leverage is stable and moderate, but net leverage sits above the issuer's own sustained target and falls only if debt reduction continues. - Coverage. Evidence: the interest cover chart table. Mechanic: lower debt reduced interest paid, lifting nine-month cover, while EBITDA declined. Implication: coverage is comfortable and improving on the available basis; the LTM cash interest ratio cannot be completed. - Cash flow quality. Evidence: the cash flow table. Mechanic: capital expenditure rose faster than cash from operations fell, working capital absorbed cash in the first and third quarters in line with seasonality described in R3 page:8, and Q3 2026 free cash flow was negative. Implication: shareholder returns and debt repayment this year exceed internally generated free cash flow; the shortfall was met from cash, which is now low. - Liquidity. Evidence: the liquidity chart table. Mechanic: available liquidity is mostly undrawn revolver; letters of credit on the revolver rose from US$51 million at March 31, 2026 to US$60 million at September 30, 2026 and consume its availability, while letters of credit on the other two facilities fell; commitments of US$43 million step down in June 2027. Implication: liquidity is adequate but revolver-dependent, and the contested tax reassessment would draw on it. - Data quality. Evidence: the CP-0 conflicts. Mechanic: all statements are unaudited; the nine-month net earnings percentage change is printed with opposite signs on R3 page:2 and page:9 (the change is a decrease); Q2 2026 diluted loss per share exceeds basic. Implication: use amounts, not printed percentages, and do not rely on Q2 2026 per-share data. - Definition risks. Evidence: the definitions table. Mechanic: Adjusted EBITDA is after cash-settled share-based compensation and includes upfront customer payments; covenant EBITDA is undisclosed. Implication: covenant headroom is reported rather than verified. - Key gaps. Evidence: the gap table below. Mechanic: absent annual statements and debt agreements remove the audited base and the legal terms. Implication: committee conclusions on structure, guarantees and recoveries cannot rest on this pack.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The supplied sources describe a publicly listed Canadian contract driller with no sponsor, no parent and no disclosed controlling holder, and with no acquisition, disposal, recapitalisation or new debt issue in the period. The business is two segments: Contract Drilling Services, which earns day-rate revenue from drilling rigs in Canada, the United States and the Middle East, and Completion and Production Services, which earns hourly and rental revenue in Canada. Volume depends on oil and gas prices and customer capital discipline; Canadian volume is seasonal because spring break-up halts heavy equipment moves. Term contracts add visibility, and coverage rose during 2026, but contracted rigs are less than half of the average active fleet, and in Q1 2026, the only quarter for which the share of utilization days is disclosed, term-contracted rigs generated a minority of days in both Canada and the United States, where reactivation costs are also depressing 2026 margins. Management describes a step change in United States margins in the fourth quarter; that is management language, not a result. For a creditor the operating story matters through four mechanics: oil-price-driven activity swings feed through to cash flow quickly because costs are largely variable; capital spending is discretionary but was raised twice in 2026, first for contracted upgrades and then for long-lead deliveries and a pending upgrade; international rigs are fully contracted but concentrated in two markets near a conflict zone; and capital allocation splits free cash flow between debt repayment and buybacks, with cash drawn down. The pack cannot show who controls the company, how concentrated customers are, how the notes came to exist, or what the credit agreement permits in distributions, so legal capacity and willingness to prioritise creditors are only partly assessable.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: term-contracted average rigs rose for 2026 and all international rigs are on five-year contracts (R3 pages 7 and 8), but the United States term share of utilization days fell in Q1 2026 (R1 page:8). Mechanic: day-rate revenue follows activity, which follows oil prices and customer budgets; term contracts floor part of it and shortfall payments are small. Implication: a commodity downturn would cut United States and Canadian volumes faster than costs fall in the first months, so cash flow and revolver reliance would rise; term coverage limits but does not remove this. Counter-evidence: no conflict logged. - Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: United States reactivation costs per day rose and guidance expects a step change in the fourth quarter (R3 pages 4 and 7); share-based compensation is cash-settled and share-price sensitive (R3 page:11). Mechanic: reactivation spending is front-loaded and is recovered only if utilization and day rates hold; compensation expense moves EBITDA with the share price. Implication: current-year EBITDA understates or overstates run-rate depending on both; the fourth-quarter guidance should be monitored, not assumed. - Concentration risk. Evidence: Canada is the largest revenue market; seven international rigs are in two Middle East markets (S3 page:7; R3 page:7). Mechanic: weather, heavy oil economics and regional conflict drive large blocks of revenue; customer concentration is not disclosed. Implication: single-region shocks matter; the true counterparty concentration is unknown. - Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified; management allocates free cash flow between debt repayment and buybacks (R3 page:6). Mechanic: with no identified sponsor or controlling holder, distributions are a board policy choice, constrained by the covenants. Implication: willingness has been creditor-supportive on debt reduction, mixed on buybacks; the legal limits on distributions are not visible in this pack. - Key uncertainties. The contested tax reassessment (S3 page:12), the covenant definitions, the cause of the Q4 2025 loss and the audit-firm conflict are open items carried to the next modules.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Precision Drilling is a moderately leveraged North American driller with sound reported credit metrics but a cyclical business and a thin cash cushion. Its strongest support is reported net debt of 1.28x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, covenant ratios far inside their limits and CAD 462.5 million of recomputed liquidity. Its weakest point is free cash flow: CAD 55.7 million for nine months 2026 against CAD 104.7 million a year earlier, while debt repayment and buybacks totalled CAD 121.6 million and cash fell to CAD 23.2 million. The outcome turns on oil-driven North American activity, the United States margin recovery management guides to, refinancing of the 2028 revolver and 2029 notes, and the Canada Revenue Agency reassessment.
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

citations.quote: Precision Drilling is a moderately leveraged North American driller with sound reported credit metrics but a cyclical business and a thin cash cushion. Its strongest support is reported net debt of 1.28x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, covenant ratios far inside their limits and CAD 462.5 million of recomputed liquidity. Its weakest point is free cash flow: CAD 55.7 million for nine months 2026 against CAD 104.7 million a year earlier, while debt repayment and buybacks totalled CAD 121.6 million and cash fell to CAD 23.2 million. The outcome turns on oil-driven North American activity, the United States margin recovery management guides to, refinancing of the 2028 revolver and 2029 notes, and the Canada Revenue Agency reassessment.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Reported leverage is moderate and stable. Net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA was between 1.20x and 1.31x at the four quarter-ends from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026, and 1.28x at the latest; total debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA was 1.33x [CP-1]. The issuer targets a sustained net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of below 1.0x, so the calculated ratio is above its own target [CP-1A]. Because the debt is in US dollars and statements in Canadian dollars, the carrying value rose by CAD 22.9 million from exchange rates over the nine months even as CAD 75.1 million was repaid, so the Canadian dollar balance understates progress [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact for the reported items, Analyst Interpretation for the ratios. 2. Free cash flow weakened. The issuer's cash from operations of CAD 279.5 million for nine months 2026 funded capital expenditure of CAD 223.8 million, up 22.9% on the prior-year nine months, leaving free cash flow of CAD 55.7 million after CAD 104.7 million the year before; in Q3 2026 alone free cash flow was negative CAD 11.7 million [CP-1]. Mechanism: expansion and upgrade spending, reactivation costs and seasonal working-capital builds absorb cash while Adjusted EBITDA is lower than the prior-year nine months. Implication: shareholder returns of CAD 46.6 million and net debt repayment of CAD 75.1 million were funded partly by running cash down to CAD 23.2 million. Category: Analyst Interpretation. 3. Liquidity is adequate but depends on the revolver. The issuer reports more than CAD 460 million of available liquidity and the recomputation gives CAD 462.5 million, of which about CAD 382 million is undrawn revolver [CP-1]. Letters of credit consume revolver availability and US$43 million of commitments expire on June 28, 2027. Category: Analyst Interpretation. 4. Refinancing is concentrated in 2028 and 2029. US$46 million of revolver is drawn to October 31, 2028 and US$400 million of 6.875% unsecured notes mature on January 15, 2029, about 90% of principal. Nothing in the supplied sources shows redemption terms, the notes' pricing history or the terms of the revolver's extension option [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact for dates, Insufficient Information for terms. 5. Covenants are not constraining on reported numbers: senior secured debt to covenant EBITDA of 0.14x against a 2.50x ceiling, and covenant EBITDA to interest of 10.27x against a 2.50x floor. The covenant EBITDA definition and the notes' coverage value are not supplied, so the reported ratios cannot be recomputed [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact; limitation stated. 6. Business risk is cyclical with partial contract support. Revenue is almost all day-rate or hourly; term-contracted average rigs were 54 in Q3 2026 against 40 a year earlier, all seven international rigs are on five-year contracts running into 2027 and 2028, but in Q1 2026 term-contracted rigs generated only 26% of Canadian and 34% of United States utilization days [CP-1A]. Category: Documentary Fact. 7. A contested tax reassessment is a contingent cash call. The Canada Revenue Agency denied a deduction for the 2018 tax year and proposed the same for 2019 to 2022; the issuer estimates a maximum tax liability of about CAD 155 million excluding interest, recognizes no liability, and must pay half of any assessed amount while contesting [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact; outcome and timing are uncertain. 8. Governance behaviour is supportive on deleveraging and mixed on distributions: the issuer reduced debt and targets CAD 100 million of reduction for 2026, and also allocates up to 50% of free cash flow before debt repayments to buybacks, with cash at a low level; no extraction or creditor-adverse action is documented, but legal capacity under the debt agreements is not visible [CP-1A]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

spans.text: ## Request

Issuer: PRECISION DRILLING Corp (issuer id pds; registrant "PRECISION DRILLING CORPORATION", Alberta, Canada; ticker PDS). As-of date: 2026-11-05. Evidence cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency per the run context: CAD. Current period: Q3 2026. Prior period: FY2025.

Question for this module: can the effective source set support the requested work, and what remains blocked? This module gives no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no investment opinion, and it does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. It separates source sufficiency from completion of downstream analysis.

Selected consumers: CP-1 (financial extraction), CP-1A (business and transaction context), CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis), CP-5 (evidence trace review). Report sections this run feeds: key findings, company operating model, model chart strip, financials and credit metrics, strengths and weaknesses, company profile, transaction summary.

The run context supplies identity (issuer name, ticker, sector, country), the dates, the currency and the periods. It is a settings file, not issuer evidence. Its blank fields (borrower, parent, guarantors, sponsor, ratings, quotes, deal terms, peers, market values) are unknowns, not zeros.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

Each file below is a text extraction of an SEC filing. Page numbers in this handoff are the extraction chunks shown as `page:N`, not printed page numbers. The sha256 is that of the pinned extraction file.

Coverage count: 7 of 7 issuer files, 94 pages in total. The run context (sha256 f0dfb9848210a0a45d246b6d35647f4b02f9221b88bb774a3f1ed2c749bd4a06) is settings, not evidence. The retrieval index file in the pack was ignored by CP-OS and is not a source.
### Supplied handoffs
None. CP-0 is the first module of this run and no upstream handoff exists.
### Coverage actually inspected

The 40-F cover, the Q3 2026 interim report (20 of 20 pages) and the Q3 2026 statements and notes (13 of 13 pages) were read in full. For the Q1 2026 report, the Q2 2026 release, the Q1 2026 statements and the Q2 2026 statements (57 pages), this assessment read the headline pages and searched every page for debt, liquidity, covenant, audit, approval, subsequent-event, restatement, amendment and guarantee terms, and opened each locator cited below. The remaining pages of those four files are retained evidence but were not individually read here; they are listed as a limitation in Gaps.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings support quarterly financial, debt, liquidity and covenant work on Precision Drilling through Q3 2026, with CAD statements and segment detail. They do not include the audited FY2025 statements, legal debt documents or ratings. | Medium | No audited annual statements or debt agreements are supplied, so terms such as guarantors, security and redemption rights rest on summary disclosure only. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Three quarters of unaudited 2026 statements and notes are supplied, with the prior year-end balance sheet as the only year-end comparative. | Quarterly leverage, liquidity and cash flow work can proceed; full-year FY2025 earnings and cash flow cannot be taken from statements. | High |

| The 40-F is a cover wrapper; its annual information form, annual report and audited statements are not in the pack. | Audited FY2025 figures, annual debt maturity detail and annual risk disclosure remain unsupported. | High |

| Debt is disclosed only as summary tables and notes: one senior credit facility and one series of unsecured senior notes. | Instrument terms beyond the tables, including guarantors and security, cannot be confirmed from filings supplied. | Medium |
| The 40-F names one auditor while the interim reports name another. | Unresolved; the audit-quality and engagement history for FY2025 cannot be established from this pack. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for each selected consumer. The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. The pack gives the owner of each selected module a located, filed evidence base for the current period (Q3 2026 and the interim periods leading to it): consolidated statements, segment tables, a debt note with facility-level carrying values, a covenant table, a liquidity table, a contingency note and a capital commitment note. The strongest contrary evidence is that none of the audited FY2025 documents named on the 40-F exhibit list are in the pack, no executed financing document is supplied, and no rating or market-price source is supplied. Source risk mechanism: where a downstream module needs an annual period or a legal term, it can only quote management summaries, which are attributed supporting claims and cannot override a filed statement or an executed agreement. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED because each owner can perform its method with bounded gaps; the gaps below must be carried into every downstream answer.

### Debt, liquidity and covenant evidence located

- Debt note: the Q3 statements list `Senior Credit Facility:` borrowings and `6.875% senior notes due 2029` and reconcile the movement in long-term debt (pages 8 and 9). No current portion of long-term debt line appears on the balance sheet (page:1).

- Liquidity table: Q3 report pages 12 and 13 give the facility, its availability and maturity. The senior credit facility matures `October 31, 2028`, with a footnote that `US$43 million will expire on June 28, 2027.` (page:13). The operating and demand letter of credit facilities are secured; the senior notes are unsecured, per the same table.

- Covenants: the senior credit facility tests a leverage ratio of senior secured debt to covenant EBITDA and an interest coverage ratio, with reported values in the covenant table (Q3 report page:13 and Q3 statements page:9). The notes carry an incurrence-based interest coverage test described on page:13 of the Q3 report. Reported covenant values exist for March 31, 2026 (page:10 of the Q1 report), June 30, 2026 (page:8 of the Q2 statements) and September 30, 2026.
- Fair value of the notes is disclosed in Note 11 (page:11 of the Q3 statements).

- Contingency: a Canada Revenue Agency reassessment matter with a stated maximum exposure and a requirement to pay part of any assessed amount while contested is described in the Q3 report (pages 11 and 12) and in Note 12 of the Q3 statements (pages 12 and 13). It first appears as a subsequent event in the Q2 release (page:6).
- Capital commitments are in Note 10 (page:11 of the Q3 statements) and the Q3 report (page:8).

### Financial base view

The reported financial base is usable for the current-period credit view at the level of consolidated quarterly statements, but it is built on unaudited interim reports and a single year-end balance sheet, so every annual figure used here is assembled from quarters rather than read from an annual statement. Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA grew in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025, while nine-month Adjusted EBITDA is lower than the prior-year nine months, because of lower upfront capital payments in Canada, higher operating costs in the United States and internationally, and higher share-based compensation (R3 page:5). Debt is a single secured revolving facility drawn in US dollars and one series of US dollar unsecured senior notes, with no current portion of long-term debt on the balance sheet. Because the debt is US dollar denominated and the statements are in Canadian dollars, reported debt moves with the exchange rate independently of repayment. Leverage computed from reported figures is steady and moderate, interest cover on a nine-month basis improved, and covenant headroom is wide. The limits are equally clear: free cash flow weakened as capital spending rose, cash is small, liquidity is revolver-dependent, a contested tax reassessment is a contingent cash call, and the annual comparators, the covenant EBITDA definition and the facility pricing are not in the pack. ### Subsequent events and contingency story

- In late July 2026, after the Q2 balance sheet date and before the Q2 release, the Canada Revenue Agency issued a Notice of Reassessment for the 2018 tax year denying a deduction of intercompany dividends received in a preferred share financing, with a proposal for the 2019 to 2022 tax years on the same basis (R2 page:6; S3 page:12). The issuer will object and says its filing position is appropriate. It expects reassessments for the 2019 to 2023 years over the next twenty-four months and does not expect taxes payable to be affected until the 2024 to 2027 tax years. Once reassessed it must pay half of the assessed tax and interest while the issue is resolved. Credit mechanism: a cash call that would arrive before resolution, without a recognized provision.

- On October 27, 2026 the issuer raised its 2026 capital budget range and disclosed a pending customer upgrade with contracts through 2029 (R3 page:2 and page:8). Shares outstanding at that date were 12,538,736 (R3 page:14) against 12,585,648 at September 30, 2026 (S3 page:10).
- With Q2 results the issuer announced a further five-year Kuwait contract for an existing rig (R2 page:2); this is a Q2 development, not an event after the Q3 balance sheet date.
### Narrative review by dimension
Each item gives evidence, risk mechanic and credit implication. Figures are in the tables above.

- Leverage. Evidence: the leverage chart table and the debt movement reconciliation. Mechanic: debt in US dollars is revalued in Canadian dollars each period, so carrying value fell by less than the net repayment because the foreign exchange adjustment added back; EBITDA recovered in Q3 2026 while cash fell, so net leverage rose from June 30, 2026 even though debt was flat. Implication: leverage is stable and moderate, but net leverage sits above the issuer's own sustained target and falls only if debt reduction continues.

- Coverage. Evidence: the interest cover chart table. Mechanic: lower debt reduced interest paid, lifting nine-month cover, while EBITDA declined. Implication: coverage is comfortable and improving on the available basis; the LTM cash interest ratio cannot be completed.

- Cash flow quality. Evidence: the cash flow table. Mechanic: capital expenditure rose faster than cash from operations fell, working capital absorbed cash in the first and third quarters in line with seasonality described in R3 page:8, and Q3 2026 free cash flow was negative. ### Business and transaction view

The supplied sources describe a publicly listed Canadian contract driller with no sponsor, no parent and no disclosed controlling holder, and with no acquisition, disposal, recapitalisation or new debt issue in the period. The business is two segments: Contract Drilling Services, which earns day-rate revenue from drilling rigs in Canada, the United States and the Middle East, and Completion and Production Services, which earns hourly and rental revenue in Canada. Volume depends on oil and gas prices and customer capital discipline; Canadian volume is seasonal because spring break-up halts heavy equipment moves. Term contracts add visibility, and coverage rose during 2026, but contracted rigs are less than half of the average active fleet, and in Q1 2026, the only quarter for which the share of utilization days is disclosed, term-contracted rigs generated a minority of days in both Canada and the United States, where reactivation costs are also depressing 2026 margins. Management describes a step change in United States margins in the fourth quarter; that is management language, not a result. For a creditor the operating story matters through four mechanics: oil-price-driven activity swings feed through to cash flow quickly because costs are largely variable; capital spending is discretionary but was raised twice in 2026, first for contracted upgrades and then for long-lead deliveries and a pending upgrade; international rigs are fully contracted but concentrated in two markets near a conflict zone; and capital allocation splits free cash flow between debt repayment and buybacks, with cash drawn down. The pack cannot show who controls the company, how concentrated customers are, how the notes came to exist, or what the credit agreement permits in distributions, so legal capacity and willingness to prioritise creditors are only partly assessable.

### Credit translations

- Revenue durability. Evidence: term-contracted average rigs rose for 2026 and all international rigs are on five-year contracts (R3 pages 7 and 8), but the United States term share of utilization days fell in Q1 2026 (R1 page:8). Mechanic: day-rate revenue follows activity, which follows oil prices and customer budgets; term contracts floor part of it and shortfall payments are small. Implication: a commodity downturn would cut United States and Canadian volumes faster than costs fall in the first months, so cash flow and revolver reliance would rise; term coverage limits but does not remove this. Counter-evidence: no conflict logged.

- Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: United States reactivation costs per day rose and guidance expects a step change in the fourth quarter (R3 pages 4 and 7); share-based compensation is cash-settled and share-price sensitive (R3 page:11). Mechanic: reactivation spending is front-loaded and is recovered only if utilization and day rates hold; compensation expense moves EBITDA with the share price. Implication: current-year EBITDA understates or overstates run-rate depending on both; the fourth-quarter guidance should be monitored, not assumed.

- Concentration risk. Evidence: Canada is the largest revenue market; seven international rigs are in two Middle East markets (S3 page:7; R3 page:7). Mechanic: weather, heavy oil economics and regional conflict drive large blocks of revenue; customer concentration is not disclosed. Implication: single-region shocks matter; the true counterparty concentration is unknown.

- Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified; management allocates free cash flow between debt repayment and buybacks (R3 page:6). Mechanic: with no identified sponsor or controlling holder, distributions are a board policy choice, constrained by the covenants. Implication: willingness has been creditor-supportive on debt reduction, mixed on buybacks; the legal limits on distributions are not visible in this pack.
- Key uncertainties. The contested tax reassessment (S3 page:12), the covenant definitions, the cause of the Q4 2025 loss and the audit-firm conflict are open items carried to the next modules.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Precision Drilling has moderate reported leverage of 1.28x net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA, wide covenant headroom and CAD 462.5 million of liquidity, but weakening free cash flow, thin cash and a contested tax reassessment leave the view cyclical. | Medium | Audited annual statements, debt agreements, customer data and ownership information are not supplied, so legal terms and concentration cannot be tested. |

### Credit view

Precision Drilling is a moderately leveraged North American driller with sound reported credit metrics but a cyclical business and a thin cash cushion. Its strongest support is reported net debt of 1.28x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, covenant ratios far inside their limits and CAD 462.5 million of recomputed liquidity. Its weakest point is free cash flow: CAD 55.7 million for nine months 2026 against CAD 104.7 million a year earlier, while debt repayment and buybacks totalled CAD 121.6 million and cash fell to CAD 23.2 million. The outcome turns on oil-driven North American activity, the United States margin recovery management guides to, refinancing of the 2028 revolver and 2029 notes, and the Canada Revenue Agency reassessment.
### Key findings

1. Reported leverage is moderate and stable. Net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA was between 1.20x and 1.31x at the four quarter-ends from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026, and 1.28x at the latest; total debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA was 1.33x [CP-1]. The issuer targets a sustained net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of below 1.0x, so the calculated ratio is above its own target [CP-1A]. Because the debt is in US dollars and statements in Canadian dollars, the carrying value rose by CAD 22.9 million from exchange rates over the nine months even as CAD 75.1 million was repaid, so the Canadian dollar balance understates progress [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact for the reported items, Analyst Interpretation for the ratios.

2. Free cash flow weakened. The issuer's cash from operations of CAD 279.5 million for nine months 2026 funded capital expenditure of CAD 223.8 million, up 22.9% on the prior-year nine months, leaving free cash flow of CAD 55.7 million after CAD 104.7 million the year before; in Q3 2026 alone free cash flow was negative CAD 11.7 million [CP-1]. Mechanism: expansion and upgrade spending, reactivation costs and seasonal working-capital builds absorb cash while Adjusted EBITDA is lower than the prior-year nine months. Implication: shareholder returns of CAD 46.6 million and net debt repayment of CAD 75.1 million were funded partly by running cash down to CAD 23.2 million. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

3. Liquidity is adequate but depends on the revolver. The issuer reports more than CAD 460 million of available liquidity and the recomputation gives CAD 462.5 million, of which about CAD 382 million is undrawn revolver [CP-1]. Letters of credit consume revolver availability and US$43 million of commitments expire on June 28, 2027. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

4. Refinancing is concentrated in 2028 and 2029. US$46 million of revolver is drawn to October 31, 2028 and US$400 million of 6.875% unsecured notes mature on January 15, 2029, about 90% of principal. Nothing in the supplied sources shows redemption terms, the notes' pricing history or the terms of the revolver's extension option [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact for dates, Insufficient Information for terms.

5. Covenants are not constraining on reported numbers: senior secured debt to covenant EBITDA of 0.14x against a 2.50x ceiling, and covenant EBITDA to interest of 10.27x against a 2.50x floor. The covenant EBITDA definition and the notes' coverage value are not supplied, so the reported ratios cannot be recomputed [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact; limitation stated.

6. Business risk is cyclical with partial contract support. Revenue is almost all day-rate or hourly; term-contracted average rigs were 54 in Q3 2026 against 40 a year earlier, all seven international rigs are on five-year contracts running into 2027 and 2028, but in Q1 2026 term-contracted rigs generated only 26% of Canadian and 34% of United States utilization days [CP-1A]. Category: Documentary Fact.

7. A contested tax reassessment is a contingent cash call. The Canada Revenue Agency denied a deduction for the 2018 tax year and proposed the same for 2019 to 2022; the issuer estimates a maximum tax liability of about CAD 155 million excluding interest, recognizes no liability, and must pay half of any assessed amount while contesting [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact; outcome and timing are uncertain.

8. Governance behaviour is supportive on deleveraging and mixed on distributions: the issuer reduced debt and targets CAD 100 million of reduction for 2026, and also allocates up to 50% of free cash flow before debt repayments to buybacks, with cash at a low level; no extraction or creditor-adverse action is documented, but legal capacity under the debt agreements is not visible [CP-1A]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths.
- Moderate leverage with stability: net debt of 1.28x and total debt of 1.33x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, in a narrow range over four quarter-ends [CP-1]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
- Wide covenant headroom on reported ratios, 0.14x against 2.50x and 10.27x against 2.50x [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact.
- Low secured debt: the secured revolver carries about 10% of principal and the unsecured notes about 90% (calculation below) [CP-1]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
- Liquidity of CAD 462.5 million on recomputation, supported by a revolver with final maturity in October 2028 [CP-1]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
- Improved coverage: nine-month Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest of 7.44x against 6.03x a year earlier, as interest paid fell with lower debt [CP-1]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
- Contract support: rising term-contracted rigs and full contracting of international rigs [CP-1A]. Category: Documentary Fact.
- Deleveraging record: debt reduced by CAD 610 million since the start of 2022 against a target of CAD 700 million through 2027, per the issuer [CP-1A]. Category: Management Language.

- Flexible capital spending: expansion and upgrade spending of CAD 84.6 million for nine months 2026 is discretionary against maintenance and infrastructure of CAD 139.3 million [CP-1]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
Weaknesses.
- Cyclical, commodity-driven activity with seasonality in Canada, the largest market, and exposure to customer budgets [CP-1A]. Category: Documentary Fact.
- Free cash flow decline and a negative Q3 2026, with a thin cash balance of CAD 23.2 million [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact.
- Revolver dependence for liquidity, with letters of credit consuming availability [CP-1]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
- Refinancing concentration: about 90% of principal in one January 2029 maturity [CP-1]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
- United States margin pressure from rig reactivation costs, with the fourth-quarter step change a management claim [CP-1A]. Category: Management Language.
- Earnings quality: Adjusted EBITDA is after cash-settled share-based compensation that follows the share price, and the covenant definition is not supplied [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact.
- Contingent tax liability of about CAD 155 million excluding interest, unrecognized [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact.

- Information limits: unaudited interim basis, no annual statements, no debt agreements, no ownership or customer data, and an unresolved auditor-name conflict [CP-0]. Category: Insufficient Information.
- Concentration: seven international rigs in two Middle East markets, with customer concentration not disclosed [CP-1A]. Category: Insufficient Information for customers.
### Credit assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Moderately leveraged, cyclical oilfield services credit with ample reported liquidity and covenant headroom, weakened by falling free cash flow, thin cash and refinancing concentrated in 2028 and 2029 | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, liquidity and cash flow tables; CP-1A operating model and behaviour rows |

Confidence is below High because the upstream business module records its own readiness judgment of this module as limited and the source readiness is limited by missing annual statements and legal documents.
### Thesis

Precision Drilling can service and refinance its moderate debt if North American drilling activity holds and free cash flow recovers after the 2026 capital programme, but returns to shareholders and debt reduction now run ahead of cash generation, so the credit rests on cyclical activity, the revolver and a single 2029 maturity (Analyst Interpretation).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Oil-price-driven activity decline | Day-rate revenue follows rig activity; costs are mostly variable but lag in the first months; term contracts cover a minority of North American days | Lower EBITDA and cash flow, more revolver reliance | Material |

| United States margin recovery fails | Reactivation costs depress margins until utilization and day rates rise; guidance is management language | EBITDA stays below the level implied by activity gains | Material |
| Free cash flow below capital allocation | Capital spending, buybacks and debt repayment total more than free cash flow; cash is low | Greater revolver drawing and slower deleveraging | Material |

| Refinancing concentration | Revolver due October 2028; about 90% of principal due January 2029; commitments step down June 2027 | Market access matters from 2027; cost of refinancing unknown | Material |

| Canada Revenue Agency reassessment | Half of any assessed tax and interest is payable while contested; no provision recognized | Possible cash call of up to about CAD 77.5 million, ahead of resolution | Material |
| Information and definition risk | Unaudited basis, undisclosed covenant EBITDA, no debt agreements | Headroom cannot be verified; legal capacity unknown | Material |
| International concentration | Seven rigs in two Middle East markets; recontracting from 2027 | Earnings concentration and geopolitical cost pressure | Minor |
| Exchange-rate translation | US dollar debt revalued in Canadian dollars; net investment hedge reduces earnings effect | Reported Canadian dollar leverage moves independently of repayment | Minor |
| Share-based compensation volatility | Cash-settled plans track the share price | Adjusted EBITDA swings with the share price | Minor |
